highlightAliases.old: Fecal occult blood screening: approximately 10 years to prevent 1 colorectal-cancer death per 1000 people; serious complications are also approximately 1 in 1000 (p161).
highlightAliases.new: Fecal occult blood screening takes approximately 10 years to prevent 1 colorectal-cancer death per 1000 screened. Serious harm comes chiefly from downstream procedures, including bleeding or perforation during colonoscopy (p161).

highlightAliases.old: Flexible sigmoidoscopy has a similar estimated time-to-benefit; the chapter notes that mortality timing for colonoscopy awaits ongoing trials (p161).
highlightAliases.new: Flexible sigmoidoscopy has a similar estimated time to benefit (p161). In the later COLONPREV trial of adults aged 50–69, invitation to biennial FIT was noninferior to invitation to one-time colonoscopy for colorectal cancer mortality at ten years. That comparison does not give a time to benefit versus no screening. COLONPREV, 2025.
